why:
MERGED 2026-09-07 during the phase-428 W10 rebase onto main, from two independent rows that both landed -- main's and this branch's. JSON keeps the LAST key, so one author's reasoning was being discarded silently. Both reached the same verdict; the prose is combined here and neither is lost.

phase-417 W4.d — `nros-log`'s emission surface, now re-exported from the `nros` facade. Before this it was reachable only as a crate dependency, and `nros::Logger` bound a DIFFERENT type (`nros_core::logger::Logger`) that forwards to the `log` crate and never reaches `nros_platform_log_write`. That is why `std::println!` was the path of least resistance from the facade, and `std::println!` is FATAL on Zephyr native_sim (issue 0589: the write recurses through `zvfs_write` and exhausts the stack with no message).

rclrs has no correspondent for the sink, arena and throttle-state types: its logging is `rclrs::log!` over rcutils, which owns its own storage. Ours are the storage, because an arena with a compile-time bound is what replaces an allocator. The MACROS mirror rclcpp's severity family rather than rclrs's single `log!`, since that is the shape a porting user writes; the `*_throttle_at` variants take the caller's `now_ns` because a target without `platform-clock` has no time base and a throttle with no clock admits everything -- so that configuration is a `compile_error!`, not a silent pass-through.

issue 1175 — this row was keyed `rust:throttle_admits` until issue 1152 renamed the function to `throttle_decide` and changed what it returns: a `bool` "may this be emitted" became `Option<u64>`, `Some(new_state)` to admit and `None` to suppress, so the caller stores the state the decision produced instead of deriving one. The sentinel moved out of the timestamp domain into bit 0 of the word (`(last_ns << 1) | ARMED`), which is what makes a STUCK clock admit once and then stay shut — the case 1152 measured, where a clock pinned at 0 admitted every record. rclrs still has no correspondent: rcutils owns its own throttle storage, ours is caller-owned because one zero-initialised `uint64_t` is what a C site can carry with no initialiser and no allocator.

The ledger kept the OLD key and gained no new one, so the gate reported `throttle_decide` UNLEDGERED and said nothing about the stale `throttle_admits` — the authored-map drift CLAUDE.md already records for this file, and issues 1042 and 1091 for the ledger generally.

`pub const fn throttle_decide(state: u64, now_ns: u64, interval_ns: u64) -> Option<u64>` in `packages/core/nros-log/src/throttle.rs` -- the throttle RULE as a pure function, one implementation behind both storages: Rust's `ThrottleState` (the `nros_*_throttle!` macros) and the C macros' zero-initialised `static uint64_t` (`packages/api/nros-c/src/log.rs` calls it for `nros_*_throttle_at`). It exists because of issue 1152 (PR #632): the `never emitted` sentinel lived in the TIMESTAMP domain, so a clock stuck at `0` -- which is what every build without `platform-clock` reports, see `rust:ThrottleClock` -- admitted every record, a flood exactly when a flood is most likely. The rule now encodes the state word as `(last_ns << 1) | ARMED`: bit 0 is the emitted flag, 63 bits of timestamp above it, elapsed time measured mod 2^63 so a wrapping counter still measures real elapsed time across the wrap. Returning the NEXT WORD rather than a `bool` is what keeps the encoding in one place -- a caller cannot admit with this rule and then arm with a different spelling of `last emitted`, which is what 1152 was. Public because the macros expand it in user crates and because the C shim must decide with the same rule (RFC-0089: a second spelling is free, a second code path is not). rclrs has nothing at this altitude: its throttle is `LogOccurrence`/`LogParams` (`rust:LogParams`, `rust:Logger::*_throttle`) around a `std` clock it picks itself, with unsynchronised state; ours is the `no_std` rule a 32-bit target with no `AtomicU64` can run from an ISR (see `rust:ThrottleClock` for why the caller supplies the clock).
